title: Immune control of lethal Nipah virus infection: the critical role of host macrophages
abstract: Abstract Nipah virus (NiV) is highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus of Henipaviru s genus that causes recurrent human outbreaks in South-East Asia, with a lethality of 40-75%. Immunopathogenesis associated to this emerging virus is still poorly understood and the role of different components of the immune response in the control of infection remains unknown. In contrast to many other mammalian species, wild type mice are resistant to NiV infection, due to an efficient type-I interferon response. We have analysed the role of various immune cell populations in the control of NiV infection and demonstrated the critical role of T lymphocytes but neither B lymphocytes nor NK cells were primordial. In addition, the depletion of phagocytes in mice by injection of clodronate liposomes resulted in dramatical increase of their susceptibility to NiV infection. Moreover, using CD169-DTR transgenic mice we show here that the specific depletion of CD169 + macrophages results in an increased susceptibility of mice to NiV challenge, highlighting the important role of this cell population. Finally, in NiV-infected African green monkeys, which closely resemble severe human Nipah disease, the production of virus-induced type-I and -II interferons was followed with an important increase of CD169 + cells in the blood and lungs, with some of them being NiV-infected. As CD169 + macrophages have been described to play an important role at the crossroads between innate and adaptive immunity in various infections, these results reveal their potentially determining role during NiV infection as well, which may help to better understand this highly lethal infectious disease.

title: Competitive inhibition of the Nipah virus matrix protein by conivaptan: from binding pocket dynamics to protein–membrane interactions
abstract: The recurrent outbreaks of Nipah virus since its first emergence have intensified efforts to identify effective antiviral therapeutics. The matrix protein is a key structural protein that maintains virion architecture and plays a crucial role in anchoring the virus to the host plasma membrane. Binding of phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to the matrix protein promotes conformational changes that facilitate membrane association and initiate viral assembly. Therefore, an effective small-molecule inhibitor should not only compete with PIP2 for binding to the Nipah virus matrix protein (NiVM) but also disrupt its interaction with the host membrane. Using virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs combined with ensemble docking, we identified conivaptan as a potential inhibitor of the Nipah virus matrix protein. The multivalent interactions of conivaptan establish stable binding within the PIP2-binding pocket while simultaneously rewiring protein-membrane interactions. In the presence of PIP2, NiVM anchors to the membrane through multiple charged residues, resulting in pronounced local bilayer deformation, an early signature of membrane remodeling. In contrast, conivaptan binding weakens membrane anchoring and preserves a more ordered and compact bilayer, thereby suppressing membrane deformation. Together, these findings identify conivaptan as a promising repurposable inhibitor of the Nipah virus matrix protein and provide a mechanistic framework for targeting virus-membrane interactions during viral assembly.

title: Vertical Transmission of Nipah Virus in an Experimentally Infected Nonhuman Primate: A Brief Report and Description of Histopathological Lesions.
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic henipavirus that causes severe, often fatal disease in humans and animals. African green monkeys have been used extensively to investigate NiV disease and are the only nonhuman primate model that accurately recapitulates human NiV pathogenesis. Here, we describe histopathological lesions in the reproductive tissues of an incidentally pregnant female African green monkey that succumbed to NiV disease. We employed multiplex immunohistochemistry techniques to profile specific cell populations that identified NiV antigen in both maternal and fetal cells of the placenta, which has not been previously described in nonhuman primate models of NiV disease.

title: Characterization of Nipah Virus Strains Malaysia and Bangladesh in a Hamster Aerosol-Exposure Model
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is an enveloped, single-stranded, negative-sense virus that causes severe respiratory distress and neurological disease in humans. While NiV disease is associated with high mortality rates (40–70%), no FDA-approved medical countermeasures (MCM) against NiV currently exist. Phylogenetic analyses have clustered isolates from Malaysia (NiV-M) and Bangladesh (NiV-B) into two distinct circulating strains associated with unique transmission routes, clinical manifestations, and lethality rates in humans. Predominantly spread by zoonotic transmission, NiV-M yields lower case-fatality rates, mild respiratory symptoms, and severe neurological manifestations. In contrast, NiV-B showcases higher case-fatality rates, marked respiratory disease, and human-to-human transmission via respiratory secretions. NiV hamster models utilizing aerosol, oronasal, intranasal, intracranial, and intraperitoneal inoculations exist. However, aerosol infection of NiV-B in hamsters remains poorly understood, while direct strain comparisons using aerosolization as an inoculation route have yet to be performed. To establish a Syrian golden hamster model comparing NiV strain-specific disease presentations and pathologies following aerosol exposure for downstream MCM characterization, we infected SGHs with a range of NiV-M and NiV-B aerosol inocula, determined the median lethal dose (LD50) and survival curves, and further elucidated both histopathological changes and viral antigen distribution within the brain and lungs. We found increased NiV-M lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease, in addition to more severe pathologies and viral signal within both the brain and lungs compared to NiV-B-infected animals. Our study serves as the first to compare aerosol exposure of NiV-B versus NiV-M in a hamster model, which can subsequently be used for crucial strain-specific MCM characterizations.

title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation
abstract: INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are increasingly investigated as host-response biomarkers for infectious diseases, but translation from differential-expression studies to clinically deployable diagnostics remains limited. AREAS COVERED: This review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika virus infection, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nipah virus disease. Unlike prior reviews focused mainly on biomarker discovery or detection technologies, it provides a cross-disease translational perspective linking miRNA signatures with analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care development, clinical implementation, economic considerations and deployment in resource-limited settings. EXPERT OPINION: The next phase of miRNA diagnostics should prioritize reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, standardized pre-analytical workflows and prospective multicentre validation rather than continued biomarker discovery alone. Clinical adoption will depend on integrating these signatures into affordable sample-to-answer platforms and demonstrating that results improve defined clinical decisions under real-world conditions.

title: Cas13d-mediated viral RNA degradation leads to potent antiviral control against both positive and negative sense RNA viruses
abstract: Respiratory viral infections continue to pose a substantial global health challenge, with a pressing need for effective treatment options. The rapid mutation rate of RNA viruses presents a significant risk of escape from existing treatments. Here, we harness the rapid adaptability and high sequence specificity of the RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13 nuclease technology to target and cleave the genome of different RNA viruses, disrupting replication and impairing propagation. We identified potent CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) combinations that can efficiently restrict viral replication in both pre- and post-viral exposure treatment settings. In vitro treatment with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) co-encapsulating Cas13d mRNA and crRNAs targeting coding and non-coding regions of positive-sense (+) RNA coronaviruses including SARS-CoV-2 effectively inhibited viral replication. In addition, both pre- and post-viral exposure treatments with the LNP-Cas13d/crRNA against the negative-sense (−) RNA Nipah virus resulted in 99% restriction of this highly pathogenic virus. Hence, the Cas13d/crRNA antiviral method holds promise as a potential therapeutic approach against severe viral infections caused by both (+) and (−) RNA viruses. Furthermore, the multi-locus targeting of viruses by Cas13d could offer a possibility to prevent virus breakthrough and increase the therapeutic arsenal against many emerging RNA viruses in the future.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染继续对全球健康构成重大挑战,迫切需要有效的 治疗 方案。RNA病毒的快速突变速率带来了从现有突变逃逸的重大风险。在这里,我们利用RNA靶向CRISPR-Cas13核酸酶技术的快速适应性和高序列特异性来靶向和切割不同RNA病毒的基因组,破坏复制并损害繁殖。我们发现了有效的 CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) 组合,可以在病毒暴露前和病毒暴露后 治疗 设置中有效限制病毒复制。体外 治疗 与脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 共封装 Cas13d mRNA 和 crRNA,靶向正义 (+) RNA 冠状病毒(包括 SARS-CoV-2)的编码和非编码区域,可有效抑制病毒复制。此外,病毒暴露前和病毒后 治疗 与针对负义 (-) RNA 尼帕病毒 的 LNP-Cas13d/crRNA 均导致对这种高致病性病毒的 99% 限制。因此,Cas13d/crRNA 抗病毒药物 方法有望成为针对 (+) 和 (-) RNA 病毒引起的严重病毒感染的潜在治疗方法。此外,Cas13d 对病毒的多位点靶向可以提供防止病毒突破的可能性,并增加未来针对许多新兴 RNA 病毒的治疗手段。

title: Deterministic–stochastic fractional-order modeling and optimal control of Nipah virus in hypertensive nephrosclerosis
abstract: Nipah virus is a zoonotic virus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease and is spread through pigs, bats or contaminated food. This research develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection. The model is kept positive and bounded to guarantee biological reality, and the disease-free equilibrium E p l is studied. The basic reproduction number R 0 l p < 1 implies extinction of the infection while R 0 l p > 1 implies small outbreaks developing into epidemics. These results are backed up by bifurcation analysis, global stability analysis and existence and uniqueness proofs for the solution. Real Malaysian co-infection data was used to parameterise the model, and simulations were carried out for both deterministic and stochastic fractional systems. The fractional-order parameter has significant impact on the infection rates and convergence behaviour. The memory effects and nonlocal dynamics are described by using piecewise Caputo–Fabrizio derivatives. Stochastic perturbations are considered to model random environmental effects. The parameters were changed to highlight the role of vaccination and stochasticity in disease extinction. The amalgamation of Caputo–Fabrizio fractional calculus and stochastic modelling, supported by a novel numerical scheme, offers a robust and flexible approach to simulate co-infection dynamics under uncertainty. The framework is further validated by PRCC sensitivity analysis and MCMC parameter estimation. Optimal control strategies provide to control the co-infection spread with economic feasibility. To summarize, the model provides useful insights into the interaction between hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus transmission, supporting the design of effective and economically feasible control strategies.
